summary: Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1949–1953) under Friedrich Weller, later serving there as Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.

Mangal Deva Shastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1919–1922) under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from circa 1931 to 1946.

Manik Man Bajracharya works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Tribhuvan University, HTW Berlin, and Metropolia University of Applied Sciences, his positions include roles at Build Change, HTW Berlin, Metropolia, and affiliations with Heidelberg institutions.
Manilal Patel was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg, where he studied under Johannes Nobel.

Manish Sinha is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Magadh University in 1999, served there as professor from 1996 (department head 2018–2021), and became an INTACH convener in 2021.

Manit Akkhachat works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ramkhamhaeng University (B.A., 2007–2009) and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (Ph.D., 2017–2022), and lectured at Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University in 2013.

Manjiri Bhalerao works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned master's degrees from Deccan College and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, where she became Associate Professor in 2004, and is attested as visiting faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2026.
Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore. His career includes academic posts at the University of Pisa and the University of Bologna.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University (1901–1902) and taught at Toyo University.

Manu Leumann was a linguist and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Strasbourg under Albert Thumb. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae, the University of Munich, and was professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics and Sanskrit at Zurich (1927–1959).

id: P:Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera
summary: Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and SOAS, later lecturing at Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (2020) and Universidad del Pacífico (2023).

Manuel Sassmann works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Stuttgart and Heidelberg University, and has served as a Research Fellow at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

id: P:Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno
summary: Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno was a Spanish scholar of philosophy who studied under Francisco García Ayuso at Complutense University of Madrid. He later served there as Professor of Literary History from 1876, also holding a post at Universidad Central.

Marbury Bladen Ogle was a scholar of linguistics and classical languages. Educated at Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve and Maurice Bloomfield, he held professorships and department headships at the universities of Vermont, Ohio State, and Minnesota.

Marc Aurel Stein worked in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. After earning a Ph.D. at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, he held major posts at Punjab University, Oriental College, and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. in 2016 at the University of Lausanne, studying under Johannes Bronkhorst and Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein, having also studied under Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. Over his career, he held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1919–1954), the University of Paris, and L'Humanité.

Marcel Granet was a Sinologist and scholar of religions educated at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held professorships at the EPHE, INALCO, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, which he co-founded.

Marcel Hofinger was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven, where he later became an ordinary professor of Greek language and literature, also serving as professor at Université catholique de Louvain (circa 1953–1983).
